A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Control Consistency Losses for Diffusion Bridges by the same authors. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial restructuring.

before.justification: V1 reports original simulations and quantitative comparisons for Ornstein–Uhlenbeck, CIR, double-well, cell-diffusion and Müller–Brown bridges, including ablations in Appendix C.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds further comparisons, ablations, a 100-dimensional Müller–Brown experiment and alanine-dipeptide simulations. These original results are distinguishable from the borrowed reference values in Table 5.

M1.justification: The fixed-point bridge learner, backward target recursion, weighting schedules and STL adjustments are retained; SC1/SC2 largely correspond to v1's existing auxiliary-drift choices. For alanine, v2 introduces limited procedural adaptations: including the base drift, scaling and clipping the Brownian guide, and performing multiple gradient updates per simulated batch (Appendix E.6).

E1.justification: V2 retains the original benchmark coverage and adds a Müller–Brown potential augmented with quadratic coordinates to 100 dimensions, plus transitions between C5 and C7ax conformations of the 22-atom alanine-dipeptide molecule. This substantially extends the evaluated input conditions and adds a real molecular system.

E2.justification: V2 adds evaluated BEL comparisons across the standard bridge problems and a guided-proposal MCMC reference for cell diffusion (Table 1, Figure 6 and Appendix E.4). Table 5 also adds published PIPS and TPS-DPS reference values, explicitly under different, underdamped dynamics. NGDB, SDB, FB and Doob's Lagrangian comparisons from v1 remain.

E3.justification: The added experiments introduce substantial protocols. The 100-dimensional test uses a larger network and 8,000 training steps, evaluating metrics only on the first two coordinates. Alanine uses 30,000 discretisation steps over 0.1 ps, different training budgets and hardware for CCDB and NGDB, and constrained/smoothed energy evaluation. The new drift-interpolation ablation also specifies its own learning rate and training budget; these are not revisions to all retained benchmarks.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained weighting-schedule and STL ablations, Appendix E.9 adds quantitative comparisons of general versus gradient-form neural parameterisations. Appendix E.10 tests intermediate auxiliary drifts across double-well barrier heights. The augmented Müller–Brown experiment additionally probes sensitivity to ambient dimensionality. These provide substantial new evidence about parameterisation, stability and scaling.

E5.justification: Matched quantitative comparisons retain mean and standard deviation over five runs, and the new ablation tables follow the same convention. No increase in repeated runs, new seed-reporting practice, confidence intervals or significance-testing procedure is established.

E6.justification: Most matched benchmark values remain unchanged, including the original Table 1 rows and two-dimensional Müller–Brown results. V2 adds BEL scores, further runtimes, molecular and 100-dimensional results, and new ablation entries. It also corrects the average-schedule double-well entry from 0.150±0.078 in v1 Table 3 to 0.148±0.073 in v2 Table 6. Results from the added settings do not establish same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: V2 adds a broader matrix-based self-consistency relation in Appendix D.3 and formal SOC extensions with nonzero running costs, including Theorems F.1–F.2 and reparameterisation derivations. V1 Appendix B.5 only outlined these connections. V2 also corrects the OU control formula (v1 Equation 36; v2 Equation 78). The new SOC appendix contains an internal inconsistency: its positive-gradient terminal condition conflicts with its exp(-g) convention.

C1.justification: The central claims about learning diffusion bridges through self-consistency without differentiating through trajectories remain. V2 adds an explicit contribution in the abstract and introduction concerning extension to general stochastic optimal control, developing what v1 discussed briefly in Appendix B.5. Stronger performance adjectives alone do not constitute a separate claim change.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations of dimensional scaling and SC2 as a more damped objective, and explicitly discusses possible fixed-point instability relative to NGDB. The molecular discussion adds substantive boundaries: single-mode paths, overdamped versus underdamped differences, and sensitivity of energy assessment to smoothing. These extend v1's existing ellipticity, simulation-cost and Jacobian-growth discussion.

D1.justification: V2 newly identifies JAX and NGDB's Brownian auxiliary process, and documents extensive molecular implementation details: AMBER14, OpenMM/DMFF, endpoint alignment, discretisation, guiding-drift modifications, training updates and hardware. Appendix G adds asset and license links for BEL, TPS-DPS, OpenMM and DMFF. These improve documentation without establishing that the retained experiments changed implementation.

R1.justification: The diffusion-bridge positioning is retained, while Appendix F substantially develops the relationship to adjoint matching, SOCM and unweighted SOCM. V2 also incorporates molecular transition-path research and newer adjoint-sampling work, including Holdijk, Seong, Havens, Liu and Choi. This broadens the substantive research context beyond a limited citation update.

P1.justification: V2 extensively rewrites and expands the main explanation, separates loss construction from bridge parameterisation, and brings derivations, auxiliary-drift discussion and benchmark descriptions forward from the appendices. The appendices are reorganised into separate method, generalisation, proof, experiment and SOC sections. CCDB and SC1/SC2 terminology replaces much of the earlier naming.

P2.justification: The main text changes to two-column layout, and figures and tables are substantially reorganised. Table 1 moves into the main text and gains performance markers; the cell plots become an expanded comparator grid. New molecular panels, a SOC relationship diagram, and runtime and ablation tables appear. Existing figures are also merged, relocated or replaced, rather than all representing new scientific content.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens evaluation of the retained method: BEL and guided-MCMC comparisons broaden validation, while parameterisation and auxiliary-drift ablations test stability claims that v1 supported less directly. Fuller runtime evidence, implementation details and explicit molecular limitations improve assessability. The gains are qualified by the restricted 100-dimensional evaluation, differing molecular comparison conditions, and the terminal-cost sign inconsistency in Appendix F. Nevertheless, the stronger comparative and diagnostic evidence, together with clearer exposition, provides a substantial net improvement.
